unregistered.heading: Codes on audit rows that the table does not hold
unregistered.note: These were recorded as given rather than dropped, so that the row saying the table is incomplete survives. Each one is a failure site whose code was never added to common/error_codes.js.
note.form: Every way this service can fail or refuse has a code of the form STS-<SUBSYSTEM>-<NNNN>. It is recorded on the audit row for the event and at the front of the service's log line, and it is never sent to a client — not in a body, a header or a redirect. Each protocol here already defines how it reports an error, and a client under test must see exactly that: the Client sees column says what it is sent, and the code changes nothing about it.
note.seenAfter: holds in this realm right now ({held}), so it falls as that log's cap discards the oldest, and it is zero for a failure recorded only as a log line — one that stops the service starting, and everything the remote PEP container records, since that container has no audit log of its own. A zero here is not "never happens".
note.http: STS-HTTP-0002 and STS-HTTP-0003 are what the HTTP call log records for a 4xx or 5xx response no handler gave a more specific code. A row carrying either names a failure site that is missing its own code. STS-HTTP-0001 is an unrouted path, which is an ordinary outcome.

codes.heading: Codes
note.table: The table is common/error_codes.js and this page has no control: a code is never renumbered or reused, because it ends up in alert rules and saved searches, and a condition that stops existing keeps its row marked retired. The same table is published as docs/error-codes.md, generated from the source, and this list is at GET /admin-api/error-codes with the same parameters. Paging is ?page= and ?per= (at most {max} rows a page).
